A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same coherent procedural mistake detection study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V2 reports original VLM evaluations, ablations, and a human study validating coherence metrics, including Tables 1–2 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds human PMD accuracy measurements in Appendix C.2 and runtime measurements in Appendix E.3.

M1.justification: The self-dialog procedure, NLI-based question ranking, in-context candidate generation, and DPO/QLoRA question-generation adapter remain unchanged. The reported stopping-threshold correction concerns an experimental setting, rather than a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Ego4D-PMD single-frame task and success/incomplete/wrong-verb/wrong-noun coverage. Dataset counts in Tables 3–4 are unchanged. The human and runtime studies reuse existing test and validation data.

E2.justification: V3 adds human PMD performance as a reference comparator in Section 5 and Appendix C.2. The evaluated model and algorithmic comparator sets remain unchanged, including GPT-4o, rationale-free evaluation, and diversity-based ranking.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a human evaluation of 100 test examples with three judgments each, and runtime evaluation processing the full validation set one example at a time. It also changes LLaVA's reported epsilon for coherence ranking without ICL from 0.5 to 0.05 (v2 Table 13; v3 Table 14), without establishing a rerun of the corresponding accuracy experiment.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.3 analyzes the runtime costs of ranking, ICL, and DPO across five LLaVA configurations. Existing training-data and length-penalty ablations, question-source analysis, and diagnostic cases remain; moving the cases into the main text does not add a new analysis.

E5.justification: V3 Table 6 adds standard deviations of runtime and iteration counts across validation examples. Appendix C.2 adds inter-annotator agreement using mean Cohen's kappa. Existing Spearman correlation tests are retained, and no additional model-seed or repeated-training-run protocol is reported.

E6.justification: Existing model-score tables retain their values. New results include 71.3% mean and 72.0% majority-vote human accuracy on 100 test examples, confidence of 3.52/5, and kappa of 0.572. New Table 6 reports mean runtimes including 11.1 seconds for vanilla LLaVA, 61.3 seconds with coherence ranking and ICL, and 7.74 seconds with DPO alone.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of relevance, informativeness, reference adjustment, question ranking, and the appendix length penalty are unchanged. Renaming the maximum iteration count from n to n* clarifies notation; no new theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: coherent PMD, the frame-based benchmark, NLI coherence metrics, and interventions exhibiting accuracy/coherence/efficiency tradeoffs. New evidence and explicit examples of diagnostic usefulness do not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: V3 interprets human accuracy and agreement as evidence of task difficulty and subjectivity, and uses measured runtimes to assess practical suitability. The limitations discussion adds substantive possibilities and boundaries involving multimodal observations, dynamic scene graphs, and asking users about information that cannot be reliably observed.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code/data repository link, fuller annotation instructions, and dataset-curation safeguards concerning prerequisite verbs and earlier matching actions in sampled videos. These expand reproducibility documentation; unchanged dataset counts and results do not establish that the underlying curation was revised.

R1.justification: V3 adds Cheng et al. (2025) on visually interpretable subtask reasoning and Cohen (1960) for agreement measurement. Broader research positioning remains stable. The ALFA publication update and OpenAI citation-suffix changes concern retained works.

P1.justification: V3 makes targeted prose revisions, expands the dataset explanation, integrates existing diagnostic examples into Section 5.3, and reorganizes Appendix C around two human studies. The overall narrative and main section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds the runtime table and moves v2 Figure 7's eight diagnostic examples into main-text Figure 5, reformatting them from two columns into four. Other figures and tables undergo relocation and reflow while retaining their principal displays.

improvement.justification: V3 better contextualizes benchmark difficulty through human accuracy/agreement and replaces qualitative latency concerns with measured runtimes. Fuller curation and annotation documentation, plus a code/data link, also improve reproducibility. The gains are limited: the small author/peer human study uses a different evaluation subset from the reported model scores, so it does not establish a rigorous human–model performance gap.
